exposure: participation in Bolsa Familia social protection programme
cohort: The study included 163 children with qRT-PCR and/or IgM-confirmed prenatal exposure to Zika virus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
finding: The study found that lower socioeconomic position (e.g., lower household income, higher crowding, participation in social protection programs) was associated with increased odds of microcephaly at birth and lower neurodevelopmental scores during early childhood in children with prenatal Zika virus exposure.
